narrative.overview:
SarapSulit should feel like a tidy, trusted market stall: warm cream paper under forest-green signage, with gold marking the price tags. Friendly, within reach, and the numbers always out in the open. The palette comes from the logo (forest leaf, gold grain): green means "go, sulit", gold means money and value, cream is the counter everything sits on.

It is moderately dense: many dishes, prices and filters, grouped into soft cards and pill toggles so a cook can scan with one thumb. Headings use a warm editorial serif (Fraunces) for personality; everything functional uses a plain sans (Inter). Motion is light and kind: cards rise in, the sulit meter fills, the logo's leaf sways once, and all of it switches off under reduced motion.

The look has three moods built on the same structure: Day (forest and cream), Night market (dark mode: deep green with mint and mango) and Rainy (the site turns blue on rainy days). Every new surface has to work in all three.
keyCharacteristics: Forest green and cream, with gold reserved for value and price cues
A serif for headings, a sans for UI, and a monospace receipt for totals
Pills for every control, soft 1rem cards, and a light lift on hover
Honesty markers ("≈", "⚠ Incomplete price", "+" after a cost) are part of the design, not noise
Mobile-first: a bottom tab bar on phones and a sticky frosted header on desktop
Three themes on one structure: day, Night market, and rainy

rules.name: The Green Means Sulit Rule
rules.body: Green is for good value and active state. Red and warm oranges are only for price rises and the low end of the sulit meter. Never use green to decorate something that is bad value.

rules.name: The Gold Is Money Rule
rules.body: Gold and amber mark prices, value and the one accent word in the hero. Don't use gold for generic decoration or for buttons.

rules.name: The Three Moods Rule
rules.body: Every new colour needs a day value, a Night market value (html.dark …) and a rainy value (body.rainy …), or it must inherit cleanly from one that already has them.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks, the Sans Works Rule
rules.body: Fraunces is only for h1, h2, h3 and .font-display. Numbers, prices, buttons and labels are always Inter, or the monospace in receipts.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Columns of prices use tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) so pesos line up.

rules.name: The Lift Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Only things you can tap or that float above the page get a shadow. Toggle rows, section blocks and the header use borders or blur, never a shadow.

dos: Do build on Tailwind's re-pointed green-* and amber-* classes, so the day palette, the html.dark overrides and the body.rainy overrides all apply automatically.
Do give every new colour a day, a Night market and a rainy value (The Three Moods Rule).
Do use pills for every control and 1rem cards for content.
Do keep "≈", "+", "⚠ Incomplete price" and price sources visible at full strength.
Do use Fraunces only for headings and Inter for anything with a number in it.
Do test on a 375px phone with the bottom tab bar showing, and check the toast and tour clear it.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion. The global rule turns off every animation and transition.
Do prefix new global CSS classes and JS names (for example share-, fx-, plan-), because all scripts share one global scope.
donts: Don't hide or soften an honesty marker to make a card look cleaner.
Don't use green on something that is bad value, or gold as generic decoration.
Don't add shadows to flat structure (sections, toggle rows, the header). Shadows are for tappable or floating things only.
Don't add a colour without dark and rainy overrides. It will break in Night market mode or on rainy days.
Don't use Fraunces for prices, buttons or labels.
Don't put essential actions only at the top of the screen on phones. The bottom bar is where the thumb is.
